subject: Hospitality
title: Event-Driven Demand Spikes
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Event-Driven Demand Spikes.

hook.text: When a major conference, concert, or sports event hits a city, nearby hotel rates can triple overnight. Events reshape demand.

buildup.text: Revenue managers track event calendars obsessively—conventions, festivals, graduations, holidays—months in advance.

discovery.text: A city hosting the Super Bowl sees hotel rates spike 200–400%. Revenue managers set these prices a year or more in advance.

twist.text: Events can also kill demand. A hurricane warning empties hotels instantly. Revenue managers must react to both spikes and crashes.

climax.text: Smart hotels negotiate group rates locked in well before events drive prices up.

punchline.text: Conferences raise rates, hurricanes crash them. Events are demand's wild card.

quiz.question: How much can hotel rates spike during events like the Super Bowl?
